After EPIC: one .pipeline/epic.json — the platform team handles the rest." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="90" width="1680" x="120" y="170" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP1" parent="b1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#7C3AED;strokeWidth=3" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="540" x="120" y="300" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP1Hdr" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=22;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#7C3AED" value="Standardization & Governance" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="500" x="140" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP1Body" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1E293B;spacingLeft=12;spacingRight=12" value="• <b>One contract</b> — every app describes itself the same way (epic.json)

• <b>One stage flow</b> — Download → Build → Test → Scan → Infra → Approval → Deploy → Integration

• <b>Scanning is not optional</b> — Wiz, SonarQube, JFrog wired in centrally

• <b>Audit-ready by default</b> — every run tagged with repo, app, type, env, cloud

• <b>Approval gates</b> configured by epic.json — consistent prod controls" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="500" x="140" y="370" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP2" parent="b1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#16A34A;strokeWidth=3" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="540" x="690" y="300" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP2Hdr" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=22;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#16A34A" value="Developer Velocity & Self-Service" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="500" x="710" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP2Body" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1E293B;spacingLeft=12;spacingRight=12" value="• <b>Zero bespoke YAML</b> — no per-app pipeline to write or maintain

• <b>Onboard in minutes</b> — drop in epic.json, register in the EPIC dashboard

• <b>Self-service runs</b> — devs trigger from a single web UI; no platform ticket needed

• <b>Live status & logs</b> — auto-refreshing dashboard across all your apps

• <b>Lower cognitive load</b> — teams ship code, not pipeline plumbing" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="500" x="710" y="370" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP3" parent="b1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFFFFF;strokeColor=#0078D4;strokeWidth=3" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="320" width="540" x="1260" y="300" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP3Hdr" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=22;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#0078D4" value="Multi-Cloud Abstraction" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="500" x="1280" y="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bP3Body" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1E293B;spacingLeft=12;spacingRight=12" value="• <b>AWS, Azure, SAP BTP</b> — one pipeline framework, three target clouds

• <b>Cloud auto-detected</b> from epic.json (awsAccountId / azureSubscriptionId / appType=btp)

• <b>App teams stay focused</b> — no need to learn each cloud's deploy specifics

• <b>Reusable Terraform modules</b> — battle-tested infra across AWS & Azure

• <b>Consistent secrets pattern</b> — AWS Secrets Manager backs every cloud target" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="240" width="500" x="1280" y="370" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bMetricsHdr" parent="b1" style="text;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=22;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#0F172A" value="The Compounding Effect" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="40" width="1800" x="60" y="650" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="bM1" parent="b1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#FFF8E1;strokeColor=#FF9900;strokeWidth=2;fontSize=64;fontStyle=1;fontColor=#B45309;align=center;verticalAlign=middle" value="<div style="line-height: 50%;">1<br><font style="font-size: 16px; <b>arn:aws:iam::{cloud.awsAccountId}:role/pge-epic-deployment-role</b><br>• Session name: PGE-EPIC-DEPLOY-ADO-{BuildId} → CloudTrail traces every action back to the run<br>• Short-lived target account (separation of duties from EPIC platform acct)<br>• <b>Recommended hardening:</b> permission boundary on pge-epic-deployment-role · external-id on trust policy · move ADO→AWS to OIDC federation (no long-lived ADO key)" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=10;fontColor=#1E293B;spacingLeft=14;spacingRight=12;spacingTop=4" vertex="1" parent="s1"> vertex="1" parent="s1"> <mxGeometry x="1932" y="570" width="408" height="320" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="sCloudAzBody" value="• ADO Service Connection backed by an Azure AD Service Principal<br>• Subscription scoped via cloud.azureSubscriptionId in epic.json<br>• Region from cloud.azureRegion (default westus2)<br>• Recommended hardening: <b>Workload Identity Federation</b> (no client secret on the SP) · scope role to the resource group, not the subscription · enable Conditional Access on the SP<br>• App secrets live in <b>Key Vault</b> (TF module) — App Service binds via managed identity" style="text;html=1;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontSize=10;fontColor=#1E293B;spacingLeft=14;spacingRight=12;spacingTop=4" vertex="1" parent="s1"> <mxGeometry
